summary: Ferdinand von Eckstein was an Indologist, philosopher, and historian. He studied at the University of Göttingen and Heidelberg University under Friedrich Creuzer, later serving as a member of the Société Asiatique from circa 1822 to 1861.

Ferdinand von Richthofen worked in history and archaeology. After studying at the University of Breslau and Humboldt University of Berlin, he held posts at the University of Bonn, University of Leipzig, and Humboldt University of Berlin.

Ferdinando Belloni-Filippi was an Indologist and philosopher who studied at the University of Pisa and University of Bonn under Carlo Formichi, Francesco Lorenzo Pullè, and Hermann Jacobi. He held professorships at the Universities of Pisa and Florence.

Ferenc Ruzsa is a scholar in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Fazekas Mihály Gimnázium and Eötvös Loránd University, he became a Kari munkatárs at Eötvös Loránd University around 1986.

Fernand Brunner was a philosopher who completed his licence at the University of Lausanne and his Ph.D. at the University of Paris. He served as a professor at the University of Neuchâtel and taught at the University of Bern.

Fernand Grenard was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies, Tibetology, and history. He completed his studies at Sciences Po (École Libre des Sciences Politiques) and the École nationale des langues orientales vivantes (INALCO).

Fernand Meyer is a Tibetologist who held appointments at the Centre national de la recherche scientifique, the École Pratique des Hautes Études (attested 2004), and the Helmholtz Centre for Infection Research in 2016.
Fernando Jose Benetti is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Nalanda University, completing doctoral research under the supervision of Aleksandra Wenta.

Fernando Tola was an Indologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and philosopher. Educated at the National University of San Marcos, he served as a professor at the University of Buenos Aires and directed the Instituto de Investigaciones Budistas.
Filip Rucinski is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He studied at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University from 2000 to 2006 and completed an M.A. at the University of Warsaw in 2009.

Filipp Fedorovich Fortunatov was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at Moscow State University, Tübingen, Berlin, Leipzig, and Paris under scholars including Pavel Petrov and Rudolf von Roth, later serving as professor at Moscow State University.

Filippo De Filippi was an Italian scholar in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. During his career, he held academic appointments at the University of Bologna and the University of Genoa.

Filippo Marsili is a scholar of sinology, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of California, Berkeley under Patricia Berger, Corrado Pensa, Arcangela Santoro, and Paolo Daffinà, and held an appointment at Saint Louis University.
Finnian M. M. Gerety is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He earned his PhD from Harvard University under Michael Witzel and Masato Fujii, later holding posts at Yale, Brown, and Oxford.

Fitzedward Hall was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute and Harvard. He held chairs at Government College Lahore and King's College London, also serving as Librarian of the India Office.

Flavio Geisshuesler is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Lausanne, Bern, and Virginia, supervised by David Germano, and held posts at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem and University of Sydney.
Flora Blanchon studied under Léon Vandermeersch and Nicole Vandier-Nicolas, and she taught Jacques Giès.

Florin Deleanu is a Buddhist studies scholar and Indologist. He studied at Bucharest, Waseda, Peking, and Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen, later serving as a professor at Kansai Medical University and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies.

Florinda De Simini is an Indologist who studied at the University of Turin under Francesco Sferra, Harunaga Isaacson, and Peter C. Bisschop. She became an Associate Professor at the University of Naples "L'Orientale."

Fokke Sierksma was a scholar of religious studies and Tibetology. He completed his Ph.D. at the University of Groningen and held positions at the University of Groningen Library and Leiden University.
